findings.title: One parent follow-up is attributed to every preceding chained agent run
findings.what: For each agent spawn, the forward scan at lines 128-135 skips all later Task/Agent calls and assigns the first subsequent non-agent call to that spawn. Thus Task(A), Task(B), Edit attributes the same Edit to both A and B. Repeated across the publication floor, this inflates both agents' produceArtifactRate and supports the concrete claim rendered at line 263 that each agent led to the parent's next move, even though only the last/active chained spawn can own that single follow-up.
findings.fix: Partition the timeline into agent-run intervals or otherwise assign each non-agent follow-up to at most one spawn; treat an earlier spawn superseded by another spawn as having no attributable parent follow-up unless the transcript supplies an explicit completion/parent correlation.
findings.acceptance: Add a regression fixture containing Task(A), Task(B), Edit across at least five runs and two sessions; verify the Edit is counted for at most one agent, the other agent's artifact rate is not inflated, and no explorer-first recommendation is published for the unsupported agent.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the nested loop independently starts at every spawn (lines 116-128), deliberately skips intervening spawn calls (lines 130-132), and reuses the same first non-spawn call (lines 133-144). The evidence-floor wrapper at lines 348-377 filters sample size but does not correct attribution, so the defect survives publication.
